verdict.line: You lose extended pokes before level 3 if you walk into Infected Cleaver range with nothing to answer it; you win the moment you land an all-in with Q's silence up, because the 51.4% head-to-head over 208 games comes from Garen's lane and solo-kill edge, not from winning poke wars.

brief.thesis: Dr. Mundo's entire kit is built to win a long fight through Adrenaline Rush regen and Infected Cleaver poke at 975 range, while Garen's kit is built to win a short fight through burst and a silence. Garen's Q (Decisive Strike) silence shuts off both Mundo's W (Burning Agony) sustain and his R (Sadism) escape for its duration, so the matchup is decided by whether Garen can force the fight to happen on his 8-second Q timer instead of Mundo's 4-second Q timer.

theirWindow.what: If Mundo has R available he can sacrifice health for a burst of Move Speed and drastically increased Health Regeneration to either disengage from your all-in or heal through it. Don't commit a long trade here unless you can kill him before the regen outpaces your damage.

yourWindow.when: right after your Q silence lands
yourWindow.what: The silence from Decisive Strike stops Mundo from casting W (Burning Agony) or R (Sadism) for its duration. Chain W (Courage) and E (Judgment) immediately in that window so his sustain and escape tools are both offline while you deal your damage.

start.why: The 59.5% win rate over 116 games reflects what this lane actually needs: AD and lifesteal to win the short trades you force, rather than flat damage reduction against a poke you're trying to close distance on anyway.

boots.why: Attack speed shortens the gap between your Q's empowered auto landing and your next full combo, and helps you actually catch Mundo instead of trading autos at his preferred range.

core.why: The active gives you a gap-close onto a champion whose kit is built to kite you with a 975-range Q; without it you're walking into Cleaver after Cleaver.
Attack speed keeps your auto-reset engine running once you're on top of him, which is the state this whole matchup is trying to reach.
Grievous Wounds directly cuts Adrenaline Rush and the healing component of his kit, which is the only thing keeping Mundo alive through your all-in.

situational.when: his passive regen alone is winning trades before you can afford Mortal Reminder
you need more durability closing distance through his Cleaver poke
you want a second burst of movement speed to finish a kill after he pops Sadism

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing rewards exactly the extended, sustained-contact fight you're trying to force onto a champion who regenerates every second, letting your trades outscale his Adrenaline Rush instead of losing to it.

summoners.why: 93.8% of players take this pairing for a reason: Ignite's Grievous Wounds removes the Adrenaline Rush regen and health-drain sustain Mundo is relying on to win the long fight, turning your all-in into a race he can't win by just waiting you out.

playing.title: Don't trade autos at his max range
playing.detail: Infected Cleaver is a 975-range skillshot on a 4-second cooldown; standing still to auto-trade just lets him land it for free while you wait for your own cooldowns.

playing.title: Hold Q for the engage, not the poke
playing.detail: Decisive Strike's silence is wasted if you fire it on cooldown at range; save the move-speed burst to close the gap and land the empowered auto as the opener to your all-in.

playing.title: Chain W and E inside the silence
playing.detail: Once Q's silence is active, Mundo cannot cast W (Burning Agony) or R (Sadism); use that exact window to land Courage and Judgment back to back.

playing.title: Respect Sadism's 75-second cooldown
playing.detail: Track when he's already used Sadism this fight or recently; if it's down, he has no Move Speed or Health Regen burst to escape your all-in or outheal your damage.

playing.title: Save R for a committed fight, not a poke
playing.detail: Demacian Justice starts at a 140-second cooldown at rank 1; don't burn it to finish a retreating Mundo when you can instead use it to open or close a fight you're already winning.

playing.title: Use Perseverance to win extended skirmishes
playing.detail: If you disengage cleanly after trading, your passive regenerates a percentage of your health per second as long as you avoid further damage, letting you re-enter the next trade healthier than he expects.

playing.title: Fight when your cooldowns are up, not his
playing.detail: OP.GG's read on this matchup holds: look to fight whenever your abilities are available, since Garen's burst window is short and punishing while Mundo's strength is the long game.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, the 51.4% head-to-head over 208 games, item and rune pick rates are measured from current-patch OP.GG data; the explanation of why those numbers happen — the silence timing, the Sadism cooldown tracking, the gap-close sequencing — is my own tactical read, not something OP.GG states directly.

stats.opponentTip: When hit with Dr. Mundo’s (Q) use [W] to either retreat or chase after him. Try to fight him whenever your skills come off cooldown to gain control over lane.
